question: If the longer baseline and its intermediate checkpoints do not qualify, does increasing TD lambda from 0.98 to 1 improve recovery with unchanged rollout length and reward?
decision: Relative to the 100-update baseline, change only TD lambda from 0.98 to 1; keep the original task/AMP 0.8/0.2 mixture and root-velocity scale 1. Evaluate all four endpoints on both impact levels/directions/backends (256 cases). An arm qualifies for fresh 120-second Stand only if both seeds show strict target-dose gain over their source, no direction/level regression, all hits Chest-first without Head, and backend admission. Assess each qualifying arm on both seeds/backends (32 additional cases per qualifying arm, maximum 320 total). Report replicated absolute recipe improvement separately from impact-practice improvement over matched quiet controls. Unassessed Stand is null, never a pass. No automatic promotion.
reuse: Verified source 120-second Stand from the earlier pilot and frozen impact baselines from Stages 3 and 5; actor identity must match. These are not new evaluation cases.
rationale: Prospective conditional branch only. Source physical failures occur 2.4002-3.7503 seconds after first contact. The pinned PPO computes bootstrapped TD-lambda returns in 64-step rollouts. At discount 0.99, increasing lambda 0.98 to 1 raises the weight of a TD residual 60 frames later from 0.1628 to 0.5472 within a rollout. It does not extend the rollout or directly bridge resets. This tests temporal credit with original reward, physics, observations, onset and 100-update budget (Stage 7 / Stage 14 update-100 reference); it does not presume a cure.
run_condition: Execute only if neither Stage 14 endpoint nor Stage 15 intermediate checkpoints qualify for replicated recipe gain with retained Stand. Otherwise use Stage 16 for independent optimization-seed replication of the qualifying recipe.
